mintAuthority.summary: ctUSD is the canonical Citrea M0-backed extension; its native wrapping routes through the Citrea SwapFacility while inherited base M issuance remains on the Ethereum MinterGateway. The M0 issuance and extension checks below are native liability controls, not bridge machinery. Current M0 Portal configuration does not authorize a direct ctUSD bridge representation, and Bridge Risk retains the reviewed Citrea native route only.

controls.label: M0 MinterGateway backing rail
controls.capDescription: Base M issuance backing ctUSD depends on approved minters, validator attestations, mint-delay review, and M0 collateral/debt checks.
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25294742: Blockscout confirms ContractName=MinterGateway, IsProxy=false (immutable, non-upgradeable). EIP-1967 admin and impl slots both zero. No external admin surface; cap governance rests with M0 TTG (POWER token holders). Native issuance checks retained from the legacy routeChecks block: M0 docs describe validator attestations before minting, although this review did not enumerate the live validator threshold; MinterGateway minting is bounded by approved-Minter status, collateral/debt checks, and mint-delay review before MToken mint; per-Minter capacity can be changed by M0 TTG governance; and the immutable MinterGateway leaves cap governance with M0 TTG and Registrar governance. These are inherited M-liability controls, not bridge machinery.

controls.label: M0 SwapFacility extension router
controls.capDescription: SwapFacility routes approved M0 extensions 1:1 against M; it can mint extension balances through wrap flows but does not create base M supply.
controls.evidence: At Citrea block 8546189: EIP-1967 proxy admin slot on 0xB6807116b3B1B321a390594e31ECD6e0076f6278 returns 0x0f38d8a5583f9316084e9c40737244870c565924 (ProxyAdmin contract, same address as Ethereum/Linea). ProxyAdmin.owner() = 0x8f4f10855fdbc3455ea1b6868d269b8fbcafd3a4 (Safe multisig, 3-of-5, owners: 0x8c9b09eb2312311bcabc4069ea2329c734e770cd, 0x028aecb628506ceb931792c89a90d45dec690a67, 0xcf4d90c0ce49e0db337b3bd8042916145d5387be, 0xa10f81bcaa44135fd15f15446b4e7531b753e698, 0x578ceb2aa7d6a02469450e4121eb4aec827f31cc). Implementation slot: 0xd87c75a92db19fe334fe7812890f893449ff1bda. Note: Citrea has a Safe directly as ProxyAdmin owner (vs TimelockController on Ethereum/Linea), reflecting Citrea's early-stage deployment. Native extension checks retained from the legacy routeChecks block: SwapFacility wraps approved M0 extensions 1:1 against M and does not create base M supply; extension minting is bounded by available M-backed wrapper flow and base M supply; the cap follows M supply and can change through the M0 governance/admin path; and the earlier review had not independently read a Citrea proxy-admin slot. These are canonical ctUSD extension issuance checks, not bridge machinery.

review.evidence: At Ethereum block 25294742: MinterGateway confirmed immutable non-proxy (Blockscout ContractName=MinterGateway, IsProxy=false). At Citrea block 8546189 (rpc.mainnet.citrea.xyz): SwapFacility EIP-1967 admin slot = 0x0f38d8a5... (ProxyAdmin); ProxyAdmin.owner() = 0x8f4f10855fdbc3455ea1b6868d269b8fbcafd3a4 (Safe 3-of-5 with 5 owners, getOwners() confirmed); implementation = 0xd87c75a9.... Safe has no modules (getModulesPaginated GS105 revert = no modules). All mint-capable surfaces confirmed. Economic-posture fields reviewed 2026-08-15: Citrea's direct 3-of-5 Safe can replace SwapFacility logic without a timelock, while the current M-backed route has real-time M0 validator reconciliation and no product-specific prudential authorization. Boundary migration (2026-08-16): the former routeChecks blocks on MinterGateway and SwapFacility describe inherited M issuance and canonical ctUSD extension wrapping; they are not bridge route checks. Current M0 Portal settings do not authorize a direct ctUSD route, so Bridge Risk retains only the reviewed Citrea native route and no bridge control is required.
